com.vector.cfg.dom.runtimesys.groovy.api

Interface ICommunicationElementSelection


  • @PublishedApi(value=ADDITIONS_ALLOWED)
 @PublishedApiDomain(value=AUTOMATION_IF)
public interface ICommunicationElementSelection
    ICommunicationElementSelection represents a selection of ICommunicationElements and the possible operations on these communication elements.

    • Method Detail

      • autoMap

        @PublishedMethod
<T extends IDataMapping> java.util.List<T> autoMap()
        autoMap() tries to auto-map the selection of ICommunicationElements (IDataCommunicationElement or IOperationCommunicationElement) according the data mapping assistant default rules. Therefore the selection of possible target signal instances is computed and tried to match to the selected communication elements. You do not have to expand the communication elements in the previous selection step. They will be expanded after the root is mapped automatically as you know from the data mapping assistant.
        Returns:
        A list of created data mappings.

      • autoMapTo

        @PublishedMethod
<T extends IDataMapping> java.util.List<T> autoMapTo(@Nonnull @VDelegatesToWithClosureParam(value=ICommunicationElementAutoMapper.class)
                                                                       groovy.lang.Closure<?> code)
        autoMapTo(Closure) tries to auto-map the selection of communication elements according the data mapping assistant rules but offers more control for the auto-mapping: Inside the closure additional predicates for narrowing down the target signal instances can be defined and code to evaluate and change the auto-mapper results can be provided. You do not have to expand the communication elements in the previous selection step. They will be expanded after the root is mapped automatically as you know from the data mapping assistant.

        autoMapTo(Closure) will produce trace, info and warning logs. To see them, activate the 'ICommunicationElementSelection' logger with the appropriate log level.

        Parameters:
        code - The code to provide target predicates or evaluate matches.
        Returns:
        A list of created data mappings.

      • getCommunicationElements

        @PublishedMethod
<T extends ICommunicationElement> java.util.Collection<T> getCommunicationElements()
        getCommunicationElements() allows access to the single communication elements in the ICommunicationElementSelection. Please make sure you are using the correct expansion mode, see ICommunicationElementSelector.selectFullyExpanded() and ICommunicationElementSelector.selectFullyExpandedButPrimitiveArraysAsLeafs().
        Returns:
        The collection of selected communication elements.

      • removePortTerminatorsForOwnerPorts

        @PublishedMethod
java.util.Collection<IComponentPort> removePortTerminatorsForOwnerPorts()
        removePortTerminatorsForOwnerPorts() removes the port terminators of the IComponentPorts of all selected ICommunicationElements.

        See terminateOwnerPorts() for more information about the purpose of terminating ports.

        Returns:
        A collection containing all component ports whose terminators have been removed by this call.

      • terminateOwnerPorts

        @PublishedMethod
java.util.Collection<IComponentPort> terminateOwnerPorts()
        terminateOwnerPorts() terminates the IComponentPorts of all selected ICommunicationElements. If one of the selected ports is already terminated or connected to another component port, the port will be ignored.

        The termination of component ports disables the validation of these ports. In other words, these ports are acknowledged as not connected yet. This should give a better overview of the open ports, which still have to be connected or need a data mapping.

        Returns:
        A collection containing all component ports which were terminated by this call.

      • unmap

        @PublishedMethod
java.util.Collection<IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResult> unmap()
        unmap() unmaps the selected communication elements from all mapped system signals. In case that not all data mappings of the selected communication elements shall be removed the mapped signal instances can be narrowed down using unmapFrom(Closure).

        For SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMappings (complex mappings) it is already enough to select one of the communication elements (for example the root element), all mappings belonging to the complex mapping will be removed. In other words removing the root mapping also removes the child mappings, removing a child mapping also removes the root mapping and the other child mappings of the same root.

        Returns:
        A collection of IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResults representing the ICommunicationElement and IAbstractSignalInstance of each removed IDataMapping.
        For IClientServerDataMappings the returned IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResult contains all details about the call signal mapping as well as the return signal mapping.
        For SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMappings (complex data mappings) the returned IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResult contains also all details about the removed child data mappings.

      • unmapFrom

        @PublishedMethod
java.util.Collection<IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResult> unmapFrom(@Nonnull @VDelegatesToWithClosureParam(value=ICommunicationElementUnmapper.class)
                                                                                     groovy.lang.Closure<?> code)
        #unmapFrom() unmaps the selected ICommunicationElements of this selection from the mapped IAbstractSignalInstances. In opposite to unmap() this method allows additional evaluation of the IAbstractSignalInstances for which the IDataMappings to the selected communication elements will be removed.

        For SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMappings (complex mappings) it is already enough to select one of the communication elements (for example the root element), all mappings belonging to the complex mapping will be removed. In other words removing the root mapping also removes the child mappings, removing a child mapping also removes the root mapping and the other child mappings of the same root.

        Returns:
        A collection of IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResults representing the ICommunicationElement and IAbstractSignalInstance of each removed IDataMapping.
        For IClientServerDataMappings the returned IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResult contains all details about the call signal mapping as well as the return signal mapping.
        For SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMappings (complex data mappings) the returned IUnmappedComElementAndSignalResult contains also all details about the removed child data mappings.
